A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FRAME-VOYAGER. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original FRAME-VOYAGER evaluations on four benchmarks, frame-selection comparisons, ablations, latency measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds benchmark results, another backbone, dynamic-selection experiments, and data-collection pruning studies.

M1.justification: The core network and ranking loss remain unchanged, but v3 introduces two substantial procedural extensions. Appendix F adds inference using normalized reward thresholds to select variable frame counts; Appendix G adds combination pruning using frame similarity, temporal proximity, and CLIP relevance. These extend v1's fixed-count selection and exhaustive combination labeling.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds evaluations on MVBench, STAR, and EgoSchema, extending coverage beyond the original four benchmarks, including camera-wearer questions in EgoSchema. The original evaluation datasets and NextQA/VideoChatGPT training sources are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated MDF, TempGQA, SigLIP, InternViT-6B, and SeViLA frame-selection comparators while retaining the earlier methods. Table 1 also adds LLaVA-OneVision-7B with and without FRAME-VOYAGER. These substantially broaden the actual comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated short-video protocol from selecting 2 of 32 candidate frames to selecting 8 of 16. v3 also adds LLaVA-OneVision-7B experiments, its selected-frame sweep through 64 frames, and dynamic-selection protocols with different thresholds and frame limits. The short-video score revisions therefore are not same-setting performance comparisons.

E4.justification: v3 adds dynamic frame-allocation analyses by duration, domain, and question type; pruning cost-versus-accuracy comparisons; a 50-example EgoSchema diagnostic; and training-data examples examining loss and visual relevance. Figure 3 extends frame-count sensitivity analysis to OneVision. The original data/layer/candidate-frame ablations and three video case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added descriptive averages and sampled case analyses do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces short-video scores under revised settings: VILA-8B plus FRAME-VOYAGER changes from 51.1 to 55.7 on ANQA and 51.6 to 60.8 on NextQA, while its Video-MME/MLVU scores remain unchanged. Numerous results are added, including dynamic VILA-8B selection achieving 49.6% with 4.1 average frames and pruning requiring 4.4% of original collection time. Table 10's short-video scores are not reconciled with the revised Table 1.

T1.justification: The combination reward, cosine frame reward, and ranking-loss equations remain unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; v3's additional confidence and efficiency explanations introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about combinational frame selection, automatic ranking-data generation, and plug-and-play improvements. The expanded experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds a specific explanation for marginal EgoSchema gains involving ambiguous pronouns and camera-wearer references, interprets adaptive frame counts in terms of information needs, and refines the loss-versus-correctness rationale. The existing formal limitations and most result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands baseline implementation instructions and code pointers, including specific CLIP/SigLIP checkpoints. Appendices F-G document adaptive thresholds, frame bounds, pruning procedures, A100 hardware, and data-collection timings; Appendix C adds memory usage. These extend reproducibility information, although pruning cutoffs remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion distinguishing continuous-segment grounded video QA from general frame-combination selection, with additional grounding, VideoAgent, and VideoTree references. Calibration and new benchmark citations are added, and BLIP-2 is removed. The central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. v3 makes localized explanatory edits, adds RQ7 and appendix subsections, revises appendix headings, and updates publication and contact text.

P2.justification: v3 expands Figure 3 into two backbone panels, adds six tables and a training-example figure, and enlarges Tables 1-2 with additional comparisons. It also rearranges analysis figures and moves v1's main video case study into the appendix. The original distribution plots and video cases are retained under revised numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through another backbone, additional learned selection comparators, and broader benchmarks. Dynamic selection and pruning directly address practical efficiency questions left unresolved by v1, while EgoSchema exposes an applicability boundary. The unexplained short-video discrepancies in Table 10 and unspecified pruning cutoffs limit that study, but the broader comparative evidence and demonstrated efficiency alternatives provide substantial overall gains.
